title: Configure Waveform crashes with KeyError: 'SIN' when the loaded circuit's waveform_params lacks the currently displayed type
steps_to_reproduce: Start from a circuit file whose stored waveform_params contains only the current type (e.g. PulseTest.json or RCCircuit.json, where waveform_params == {'PULSE': {...}}).
Open the circuit in the app (File > Open).
Click the 'Configure waveform' button in the properties panel.
expected_behavior: The WaveformConfigDialog opens with the current waveform type selected and its editable parameters populated, regardless of which waveform types are present in the stored waveform_params.
actual_behavior: KeyError: 'SIN' is raised during dialog construction (waveform_config_dialog.py:83), so the dialog never opens.
traceback:
File "...\app\GUI\properties_panel.py", line 281, in configure_waveform
    dialog = WaveformConfigDialog(self.current_component, self)
File "...\app\GUI\waveform_config_dialog.py", line 55, in init_ui
    self.create_param_inputs()
File "...\app\GUI\waveform_config_dialog.py", line 83, in create_param_inputs
    "offset": QLineEdit(self.component.waveform_params["SIN"]["offset"]),
KeyError: 'SIN'
root_cause: create_param_inputs() unconditionally reads every waveform type (SIN, PULSE, EXP) from self.component.waveform_params and wraps each in a QLineEdit at construction time. But the stored waveform_params for some saved circuits contains only the *current* waveform type (e.g. {'PULSE': {...}} in PulseTest.json and RCCircuit.json), not all three. Because the constructor reads all three keys before any type is selected, loading a PULSE-only (or EXP-only) circuit and opening the dialog raises KeyError: 'SIN'. The default freshly-created component has all three types, so the crash only occurs on loaded circuits that were serialized with a partial waveform_params dict.

evidence.serialization: models/component.py ComponentData.to_dict() writes self.waveform_params verbatim, so whatever dict the component held at save time is restored on load (component.py:from_dict lines 492-493). A component whose params were only ever set for one type (e.g. netlist_parser._setup_waveform_params only assigns a single-key dict) round-trips as a partial dict.

related_files.buggy: app\GUI\waveform_config_dialog.py lines 79-110 (create_param_inputs) - assumes all three waveform types are present.
related_files.model: app\models\component.py - to_dict (444-447) and from_dict (489-493) round-trip waveform_params without ensuring all three keys.
related_files.parsers: app\simulation\netlist_parser.py _setup_waveform_params (557-600) only sets a single-key dict (e.g. {"PULSE": ...}); app\simulation\circuitikz_parser.py line 340 does comp.waveform_params[wtype] = wparams.
related_files.defaults: app\models\waveform_defaults.py default_waveform_params() - the only place that reliably produces all three keys.

fix_options.title: Harden create_param_inputs to use defaults for missing keys
fix_options.description: In create_param_inputs(), fall back to default_waveform_params() for any missing type/key instead of assuming all three are present. This fixes the crash regardless of how the circuit was loaded, and keeps the per-type input dicts fully populated for on_type_changed().
fix_options.notes: Recommended. Adds one import from models.waveform_defaults and changes the dict-access pattern to param.get with a default.

fix_options.title: Normalize waveform_params on load to include all types
fix_options.description: In ComponentData.from_dict(), after restoring waveform_params, ensure all three keys exist by filling missing ones from default_waveform_params(). Fixes the invariant at the model boundary.
fix_options.notes: Defensive; also fix netlist_parser._setup_waveform_params to always set all three keys. Cures the root invariant rather than the symptom.

fix_options.title: Build param inputs lazily for the current type only
fix_options.description: Recreate_param_inputs() so it only builds inputs for the currently selected type (on init, call create for self.component.waveform_type), and rebuild on type change. Fewer widgets, but must still guard against an unknown waveform_type from a loaded file.
fix_options.notes: Larger change; must still guard unknown types.

test_recommendations: Add a circuit fixture (or load app/tests/data/PulseTest.json) whose waveform_params has a single key and assert the dialog constructs without raising.
Cover from_dict round-trip when stored waveform_params omits keys, to lock the model-level invariant you choose to enforce.
Cover on_type_changed switching to a type whose params were not initially loaded.
notes: A UserWarning about 'No artists with labels found to put in legend' was also in the pasted output (plot_utils.py:36); it is likely unrelated to this crash (legend called on an empty plot) and should be triaged separately.
The default freshly-created Waveform Source has all three types, which is why the bug does not appear in new circuits.
